description: How organisations decide what to protect, how much risk to accept and how to prove their security works: assets and threats, risk assessment, policy, controls, continuity, people and audit. Students work through branching case studies where they gather evidence, make decisions and are scored against a rubric.
modelledOn: ISO/IEC 27001, 27002 and 27005 information security management standards
NIST SP 800-30 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework
Whitman and Mattord, Management of Information Security
ISACA CISM and CRISC certification bodies of knowledge
outcomes: Build an asset inventory and a threat and vulnerability picture for an organisation, with business impact ratings.
Carry out qualitative and quantitative risk assessments and choose and justify a risk treatment.
Write a security policy hierarchy that is enforceable, proportionate and mapped to a recognised standard.
Select and map controls from ISO 27002, NIST and CIS frameworks on cost-benefit grounds.
Develop a business continuity and disaster recovery plan with defined recovery objectives and test it by exercise.
Plan and report an audit of security controls and communicate findings to a board.

units.title: Security management and governance foundations
topics: Security goals (confidentiality, integrity, availability) and the role of the security function and the CISO
Governance versus management; board duties and the three lines model
Aligning security with strategy: budgets, key performance indicators and key risk indicators
Legal and regulatory setting: Ghana Data Protection Act 2012, Cybersecurity Act 2020, Bank of Ghana directives and GDPR
Standards landscape: ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53 and COBIT

units.title: Asset and threat identification
topics: Asset inventory and information classification; identifying crown-jewel assets
Business impact analysis: criticality, dependencies and valuation
Threat actors, motives and capabilities; threat intelligence and MITRE ATT&CK as a shared vocabulary
Vulnerability sources: scanners, penetration test reports, CVE and CVSS scoring
Scenario building and attack trees; third-party and supply chain exposure

units.title: Risk assessment methods
topics: Risk concepts: likelihood, impact, inherent and residual risk, appetite and tolerance
Qualitative assessment with risk matrices and their known weaknesses
Structured methods: the ISO 27005 process, NIST SP 800-30 and OCTAVE
Quantitative assessment: single and annualised loss expectancy, FAIR and Monte Carlo loss distributions
Risk treatment: avoid, reduce, transfer (including cyber insurance) or accept; the risk register
Risk communication, aggregation and reporting to the board

units.title: Security policy and standards
topics: The document hierarchy: policy, standard, procedure and guideline; writing enforceable policy
Core policies: acceptable use, access control, passwords, remote work and bring-your-own-device
Data classification and handling, retention, privacy policy and data protection impact assessment
Policy lifecycle: approval, exceptions, communication and review
The ISMS: ISO 27001 clauses, scope, statement of applicability and the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle

units.title: Controls and control frameworks
topics: Control types: preventive, detective, corrective and deterrent; administrative, technical and physical
ISO 27002 and NIST SP 800-53 control families, the CIS Controls and mapping between frameworks
Selecting controls by cost-benefit and risk reduction; defence in depth
Identity and access governance: least privilege, segregation of duties and joiner-mover-leaver processes
Vendor and cloud risk: third-party assessment, shared responsibility and service level agreements
Incident response governance: roles, playbooks, notification duties and lessons learned

units.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
topics: The business continuity lifecycle (ISO 22301): MTPD, RTO and RPO from the business impact analysis
Continuity strategies: backups, hot, warm and cold sites, cloud failover and manual workarounds; power and connectivity risks in West Africa
Disaster recovery plans, runbooks and call trees
Exercising plans: walkthroughs, tabletop exercises and full failover tests; measuring results
Crisis management and communication with customers, regulators and the media

units.title: Security awareness and human factors
topics: Social engineering: phishing, pretexting, SIM-swap and mobile money fraud
Insider threat: malicious and negligent insiders, monitoring and its ethics
Why people bypass controls: usable security, behavioural models and nudges
Designing awareness programmes and measuring them: phishing simulations and behaviour metrics
Security culture, reporting and a just culture

units.title: Audit and assurance
topics: Audit types and roles: internal, external and certification audits; independence and the audit charter
The audit process: planning, evidence collection, sampling, control testing and findings
Compliance regimes: PCI DSS, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification; governance, risk and compliance tooling
Metrics, continuous monitoring and maturity models
Capstone: governance review of a regional bank or utility, producing a risk register and a board report

schedule.title: Governance, law and standards
schedule.exercise: Read a summary of the Ghana Data Protection Act and write a one-page memo listing the duties it places on a micro-lender holding customer records.

tasks.title: Match ten security incidents in a short case to the confidentiality, integrity or availability goal each one breaks.
Decide which Ghanaian and international legal duties apply to a mobile-money agent network after a customer data leak, citing evidence in the case file.
Choose five key risk indicators and targets for a bank's security programme, justify each, and defend the budget request against a sceptical board member.

schedule.title: Assets, impact and threats
schedule.exercise: Build an asset register for a district hospital (patient records, lab systems, power, staff) and classify each asset and its owner.

tasks.title: Classify 15 assets of a rural bank into public, internal, confidential or restricted and name the owner of each.
Map the dependencies of a payroll service on systems, vendors and people, and mark the single points of failure.
Profile the likely threat actors for a telecom operator from intelligence reports, ranking them by capability and motive, and choose which to plan against.

schedule.title: Vulnerabilities, scenarios and supply chain
schedule.exercise: Take a penetration test report with 30 findings and explain how you would prioritise them using CVSS together with asset value and exposure.

tasks.title: Rank twelve scanner findings by CVSS score and by actual business exposure, and explain where the two orders disagree.
Draw an attack tree for stealing funds from a mobile money platform, with at least four branches and a cost estimate for each leaf.
Assess the exposure from a compromised software supplier, gather evidence from logs and contracts, and recommend actions within the case time limit.

schedule.title: Risk concepts and qualitative assessment
schedule.exercise: Rate ten risks on a five-by-five matrix, then show with two examples why the matrix can rank a smaller risk above a larger one.

tasks.title: Distinguish inherent and residual risk for a record-keeping system before and after two controls, and place both on a matrix.
Score eight risks in a clinic scenario with the risk matrix, then rescore after management changes the impact scale, and report the ranking changes.
Set a risk appetite statement and tolerance thresholds for a savings and loans company, then test it against four proposed projects.

schedule.title: Structured and quantitative risk assessment
schedule.exercise: Compute the annualised loss expectancy for a ransomware scenario at a hospital and decide whether a backup system costing GHS 120000 per year is justified.

tasks.title: Compute single loss expectancy, annualised rate of occurrence and annualised loss expectancy for three scenarios and compare them with control costs.
Follow the ISO 27005 process step by step on a case, producing the context, risk identification, analysis and evaluation record.
Run a Monte Carlo simulation of annual loss with frequency and severity distributions, and report the mean and the 95th percentile for the board.

schedule.title: Risk treatment and communication
schedule.exercise: Prepare a five-slide briefing for a board that asks for approval of a risk treatment plan, including what you recommend the board accept.

tasks.title: Choose avoid, reduce, transfer or accept for six risks in a case and write a one-line reason for each.
Build a risk register with owner, treatment, deadline and residual score for a utility's top ten risks, and defend it against challenge.
Aggregate related risks across three departments into a board view, avoiding double counting, and answer scripted board questions scored by a rubric.

schedule.title: Writing and running security policy
schedule.exercise: Draft an acceptable use policy and a bring-your-own-device standard for a large technical college, and identify which clauses are enforceable and how.

tasks.title: Sort 15 statements into policy, standard, procedure or guideline and rewrite two that are too vague to enforce.
Draft a remote-work and password policy for a startup, then handle three scripted exception requests and record the decisions.
Prepare the scope and statement of applicability for an ISO 27001 ISMS in a given organisation, justifying each excluded control.

schedule.title: Control types, frameworks and selection
schedule.exercise: Map ten controls from the CIS Controls to ISO 27002 and NIST SP 800-53 families, and note where the mapping is not one to one.

tasks.title: Classify twenty controls as preventive, detective, corrective or deterrent, and as administrative, technical or physical.
Map eight given controls across ISO 27002, NIST SP 800-53 and CIS Controls and identify two gaps in an organisation's current set.
Choose controls for a fixed budget that reduce the most annualised loss, comparing at least six options by cost-benefit and justifying the final mix.

schedule.title: Access governance, vendors and incident governance
schedule.exercise: Review a vendor questionnaire from a cloud provider and list the five answers that most concern you and the evidence you would ask for.

tasks.title: Find the segregation of duties conflicts in a table of eight user roles in a finance system and propose a fix for each.
Assess a third-party mobile money aggregator from its audit report and contract, decide whether to onboard, and list the conditions to impose.
Lead the response to a data breach: assign roles, decide notification timing to regulators and customers, and be scored on decisions and evidence handling.

schedule.title: Continuity and disaster recovery
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page continuity plan for a district pharmacy distributor that must keep orders flowing during a multi-day power and network outage.

tasks.title: Set the RTO and RPO for five business services from impact figures in a case, and explain how each was chosen.
Compare hot, warm and cold site options and cloud failover for a bank branch network, choosing one on cost and recovery time.
Run a tabletop exercise for a data centre fire with timed injects, make recovery decisions, and be scored against the target RTO and communication plan.

schedule.title: People, social engineering and culture
schedule.exercise: Design a four-week awareness campaign for mobile money agents about SIM-swap fraud, with a measure of success for each week.

tasks.title: Identify the social engineering techniques used in five short fraud call transcripts and mark the point where a staff member could have stopped it.
Analyse click and report rates from three rounds of a phishing simulation, plot the trend and recommend a change to the training.
Investigate a suspected insider leaking customer data, weigh monitoring against staff privacy, and decide on evidence and escalation under time pressure.

schedule.title: Audit planning, testing and compliance
schedule.exercise: Prepare an audit plan for the access control domain of a microfinance company, with objectives, scope, sample sizes and the evidence to request.

tasks.title: Decide which of six reporting lines compromise an internal auditor's independence in a case, and explain each decision.
Test a sample of 25 user-access changes against the approval policy, record exceptions, and write graded findings.
Prepare a mock PCI DSS assessment for a payment processor: choose scope, gather evidence, identify gaps and negotiate a remediation plan.

schedule.title: Metrics, maturity and the governance review
schedule.exercise: Present the capstone: a risk register, control gaps, a roadmap and a board report for a regional bank or utility, defended against questions.

tasks.title: Place an organisation on a five-level maturity scale for six security domains using the evidence in the case file.
Chart eight security metrics over four quarters, flag the ones that signal a deteriorating control, and recommend actions.
Complete a governance review of a regional bank: finalise the risk register, choose priorities and present to a simulated board scored on rigour and clarity.
